def-sample-covering-number:
## Definition

Let $n,m\ge1$, let $U$ be a nonempty subset of the real matrix space $\mathbb R^{n\times m}$, and let $\epsilon>0$. A **proper $\epsilon$-cover** of $U$ in Frobenius norm is a finite subset $V\subseteq U$ such that every $X\in U$ has some $Y\in V$ with $\lVert X-Y\rVert_F\le\epsilon$. The **proper Frobenius covering number** $N_F(U,\epsilon)$ is the least cardinality of such a cover when one exists, and is $+\infty$ otherwise. The cover is proper because its centers belong to $U$.
lem-empirical-rademacher-covering-integr:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $S=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a fixed sample, and let $\mathcal G$ be a nonempty class of measurable functions into $[0,1]$. Write $\mathcal G|S$ for the set of column vectors $(g(z_1),\ldots,g(z_n))^\top$ as $g$ ranges over $\mathcal G$. For $0<\alpha\le\sqrt n$,
$$\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal G)\le\frac{4\alpha}{\sqrt n}+\frac{12}{n}\int_\alpha^{\sqrt n}\sqrt{\log N_F(\mathcal G|S,\epsilon)}\,d\epsilon,$$
where $\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S$ is the one-sided empirical Rademacher complexity with $1/n$ normalization and $N_F$ is the proper Frobenius covering number of the sample-vector set, identified with $n\times1$ matrices. The set $\mathcal G|S$ is totally bounded because it lies in $[0,1]^n$.
def-multiclass-margin-ramp-loss:
## Definition

Let $K\ge2$, let $D$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^d\times\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and let $F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^K$ be a continuous score map. At $(x,y)$ its **multiclass margin** is
$$m_F(x,y):=F(x)_y-\max_{j\ne y}F(x)_j.$$
The predicted label is the smallest index maximizing $F(x)_j$. Its population zero-one error is
$$L_0(F):=D\bigl(\{(x,y):\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\le j\le K}F(x)_j\ne y\}\bigr).$$
For $\gamma>0$, the **ramp loss** is
$$\ell_\gamma(r):=\begin{cases}0,&r< -\gamma,\\1+r/\gamma,&-\gamma\le r\le0,\\1,&r>0.\end{cases}$$
The population ramp risk is $R_\gamma(F):=\int\ell_\gamma(-m_F(x,y))\,D(d(x,y))$. For a sample $S=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n))$ of length $n\ge1$, the empirical ramp risk and empirical margin loss are
$$\widehat R_{\gamma,S}(F):=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_\gamma(-m_F(x_i,y_i)),\qquad\widehat L_{\gamma,S}(F):=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{m_F(x_i,y_i)\le\gamma\}.$$
The score coordinates are continuous, and finite maxima, comparisons, and the piecewise-linear ramp preserve Borel measurability. Thus the classification event and ramp loss in the displayed integrals are Borel sets or functions, so the risks are well-defined for $D$.
lem-spectral-network-matrix-cover:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, $M\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ with $n,d,m\ge1$, and let $a,s\ge0$. Suppose
$$C:=\{A\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}:\lVert A-M\rVert_{2,1}\le a,\ \lVert A\rVert_\sigma\le s\}$$
is nonempty. Put $U:=\{XA:A\in C\}$. For every $\epsilon>0$,
$$\log N_F(U,\epsilon)\le5\,\frac{a^2\lVert X\rVert_F^2}{\epsilon^2}\log(2dm).$$
If $a\lVert X\rVert_F=0$ or $\epsilon\ge2a\lVert X\rVert_F$, then $N_F(U,\epsilon)=1$. Here $\lVert A-M\rVert_{2,1}$ is the column-sum norm of the transpose-difference, as fixed in the spectral-network-complexity definition, and $N_F$ is the proper Frobenius covering number.
lem-multiclass-margin-rademacher-general:
## Statement

Assume the axiom of choice.

Fix a finite network architecture with $L\ge1$, widths $d_0,\ldots,d_L\ge1$, output size $K=d_L\ge2$, and activations as in the spectral-network-complexity definition. Let $s_i>0$, $b_i\ge0$, and reference matrices $M_i$ be such that the class
$$\mathcal F:=\{F_A:\lVert A_i\rVert_\sigma\le s_i,\ \lVert A_i^\top-M_i^\top\rVert_{2,1}\le b_i\text{ for every }i\}$$
is nonempty. Let $D$ be any Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{d_0}\times\{1,\ldots,K\}$, let $S=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n))$ be an independent identically distributed sample from $D$ with $n\ge1$, and fix $\gamma>0$ and $0<\delta<1$. Define the ramp-loss class
$$\mathcal L_\gamma:=\{(x,y)\mapsto\ell_\gamma(-m_F(x,y)):F\in\mathcal F\}.$$
With probability at least $1-\delta$ over $S$, every $F\in\mathcal F$ satisfies
$$L_0(F)\le\widehat L_{\gamma,S}(F)+2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}},$$
where $\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S$ is the one-sided empirical Rademacher complexity with $1/n$ normalization.
lem-spectral-network-output-covering-ent:
## Statement

Fix an architecture and activations as in the spectral-network-complexity definition, with widths $d_0,ldots,d_L$ and $W:=\max_i d_i$. Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d_0}$ be any sample matrix, let $M_i\in\mathbb R^{d_i\times d_{i-1}}$, and fix $s_i>0$ and $b_i\ge0$. Suppose each feasible layer set
$$C_i:=\{A_i:\lVert A_i\rVert_\sigma\le s_i,\ \lVert A_i^\top-M_i^\top\rVert_{2,1}\le b_i\}$$
is nonempty. Let $\mathcal H_X$ be the set of $n\times d_L$ score matrices whose $r$th row is $F_A(x_r)^\top$, for $A_i\in C_i$ and the $r$th row $x_r^\top$ of $X$. Then for every $\epsilon>0$,
$$\log N_F(\mathcal H_X,\epsilon)\le5\,\frac{\lVert X\rVert_F^2}{\epsilon^2}\log(2W^2)\left(\prod_{i=1}^L(\rho_i s_i)^2\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^L(b_i/s_i)^{2/3}\right)^3.$$
The logarithm is natural, an empty product equals $1$, and $N_F$ uses proper centers in the covered score-matrix set.
lem-bounded-spectral-class-margin-genera:
## Statement

Assume the axiom of choice.

Fix a finite network architecture with $L\ge1$, widths $d_0,\ldots,d_L\ge1$, output size $K=d_L\ge2$, activations, and reference matrices as in the spectral-network-complexity definition. Let $s_i>0$, $b_i\ge0$, and let $\mathcal F$ be the nonempty class with layer constraints $\lVert A_i\rVert_\sigma\le s_i$ and $\lVert A_i^\top-M_i^\top\rVert_{2,1}\le b_i$. Let $S=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n))$ be an iid sample from any Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{d_0}\times\{1,\ldots,K\}$, let $X$ be its input matrix with rows $x_i^\top$, and fix $n\ge1$, $\gamma>0$, and $0<\delta<1$. Set $W:=\max_{0\le i\le L}d_i$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, every $F_A\in\mathcal F$ satisfies
$$L_0(F_A)\le\widehat L_{\gamma,S}(F_A)+\frac8n+\frac{36\sqrt{20}\,\lVert X\rVert_F\sqrt{\log(2W^2)}\log n}{\gamma n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^L\rho_i s_i\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^L(b_i/s_i)^{2/3}\right)^{3/2}+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}.$$
All logarithms are natural. The matrix norm on $X$ is the Frobenius norm, and the empirical margin loss uses the threshold convention $m_{F_A}(x_i,y_i)\le\gamma$.
thm-spectral-margin-bound-for-multiclass:
## Statement

Assume the axiom of choice. Fix a network architecture with $L\ge1$, widths $d_0,\ldots,d_L\ge1$, $K=d_L\ge2$, zero-bias recurrence and zero-origin $\rho_i$-Lipschitz activations as in the spectral-network-complexity definition. Fix reference matrices $M_i\in\mathbb R^{d_i\times d_{i-1}}$. Let $S=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n))$ be an iid sample of size $n\ge1$ from any Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{d_0}\times\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and let $X$ be the matrix with rows $x_r^\top$. Fix $0<\delta<1$ and set $W:=\max_{0\le i\le L}d_i$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously for every network with nonzero layer matrices and every margin $\gamma>0$,
$$L_0(F_A)\le\widehat L_{\gamma,S}(F_A)+\frac8n+\frac{72\sqrt{20}\,(1+\lVert X\rVert_F)\sqrt{\log(2W^2)}\log n}{\gamma n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^L\rho_i\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^L\left[\left(\frac1L+\lVert A_i^\top-M_i^\top\rVert_{2,1}\right)\prod_{r\ne i}\left(\frac1L+\lVert A_r\rVert_\sigma\right)\right]^{2/3}\right)^{3/2}+3\sqrt{\frac{Q(A,X,\gamma,n,\delta)}{2n}},$$
where all logarithms are natural, an empty product equals $1$, and
$$\begin{aligned}Q(A,X,\gamma,n,\delta):={}&\log(6/\delta)+\log(2+n\gamma)+\log(2+n/\gamma)+2\log(2+\lVert X\rVert_F)\\&+2\sum_{i=1}^L\log\!\left(2+L\lVert A_i^\top-M_i^\top\rVert_{2,1}\right)+2\sum_{i=1}^L\log\!\left(2+L\lVert A_i\rVert_\sigma\right). \end{aligned}$$
